reader.notes: One framing (RecordFraming) serves every sequential file whatever the clause says, and it strips the 4-byte length word before the record area is filled. With no RECORD clause an OCCURS DEPENDING ON record is written fixed at its maximum (7 bytes, no prefix): §1985:II.2.1.4.3 leaves fixed or variable to the implementor in that case, so that is not a breach of this rule.

refuter.evidence: Probes under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-221/runs, all --std 85. What the reader did not try, and passes: rd_sizes-002 (a) RECORD VARYING without DEPENDING ON over two record sizes, READ INTO W12 -> [ABCDEFGH    ] then [XYZ         ] (group move of the current record, not the frame); DEPENDING ON long/short/long -> L=10/02/05 with the area and INTO exact; Format 3 RECORD CONTAINS 3 TO 8 (implementor-defined variable) -> same; STANDARD-1 over DEPENDING ON with READ INTO -> L=07 [PQRSTUV], L=01 [Z]. rd_reversed-001 (c, 1985-only) OPEN EXTEND then OPEN INPUT ... REVERSED of a no-clause file and a STANDARD-1 file -> XY/0123456789/ABC with L=02/10/03, then EOF 10; (e) a reader FD of max 4 over a 10-byte record -> 04, L=04 [0123]; READ after OPEN 35 -> 47, DEPENDING ON item unchanged (77). THE FAILURE: rd_print-001 (and rd_linage2-001) FC = RECORD DELIMITER IS STANDARD-1, RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON LC, LINAGE IS 20 LINES, written with BEFORE ADVANCING 2 LINES (legal: §1985:VII.4.7.3 SR3 bars only ADVANCING mnemonic-name under LINAGE) -> W 00, then OPEN INPUT of the same file through the same FD -> 39, READ -> 47: the program never gets back any record its own clause framed. RDPC.DAT = 41 42 20 20 0d 0a 0d 0a 43 44 45 0d 0a 0d 0a (unframed text, DOC-A.1-146 (c')). --std 2023 identical (rd_print-002). Cause: SequentialConnector.cs#FixedAttributeConflict answers 39 whenever a RECORD VARYING file fails RecordFraming.StreamFramingParses, and a print stream is not a framed stream; 39 is defined only for a conflict between the fixed file attributes and the program's (§1985:VII.1.3.5 item f), and here the FD is the one that created the file. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.2.8.4 GR1  (║2.8.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:II.2.1.4  (2.1.4 Logical Records)  the text is in the clause'; 'OK  §1985:VII.4.7.4 GR16  (4.7.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR16'; 'OK  §1985:VII.1.3.5  (1.3.5 I-O Status)  the text is in the clause; it lies in GRL2.3f'; 'OK  §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR11  (3.8.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR11'. DOUBTFUL, the reading stated: GR1 constrains what a SUCCESSFUL read shows (the method absent from the record area and size), and every successful read probed conforms; the defect is that the read never succeeds for a variable-length file written as a print representation (LINAGE / ADVANCING). The reader's own requirement sentence ('a READ returns exactly the bytes written and the DEPENDING ON item gets the record's length') is falsified by FC; whether that failure belongs to GR1 or to OPEN/GR4 is a reading the text does not settle. kb/Work: no note found (grep of kb/Work for print stream / StreamFramingParses / 39: PB1664, PB2509, PB484, PB2754 treat the write form and torn tails, not this read-back).
